plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three distinct strategy axes for a long-wave pass filter on HgCdTe detectors: (1) periodic quarter-wave stack efficiency with minimal layers, (2) aperiodic full-optimization with maximum allowed layers, and (3) intermediate periodic stack to test layer-count scaling. All routes use only ZnS and ZnSe on Ge substrate as specified, targeting high transmission in 8000-11000 nm LWIR and suppression in 3000-5000 nm MWIR. The axes are genuinely different: Route 1 tests whether simple periodicity suffices, Route 2 tests whether free optimization outperforms periodicity, Route 3 tests whether more periods improve stopband depth. Literature L07 and L10 directly support the Ge/ZnS/ZnSe material system for IR filters; L12 and L13 support the cryogenic detector context. No route substitutes materials since the user explicitly required ZnS and ZnSe.

routes.title: Periodic 8-layer quarter-wave stack for MWIR stopband
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic 4-pair ZnS/ZnSe quarter-wave stack centered on the MWIR band can achieve high LWIR transmission while suppressing MWIR thermal background, with minimal layer count reducing manufacturing complexity.
routes.design_principle: Bragg reflector physics: alternating high/low index layers with quarter-wave optical thickness at the stopband center wavelength create constructive interference for reflection in the stopband (3000-5000 nm) while transmitting outside the stopband (8000-11000 nm).
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | Ge substrate (8 layers total, 4 alternating pairs)
design_variables: ZnS layer thickness (applied to all 4 ZnS layers)
ZnSe layer thickness (applied to all 4 ZnSe layers)
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band
Maintain smooth spectral response without sharp ripples in LWIR passband
manufacturing_considerations: ZnS and ZnSe have compatible thermal expansion for cryogenic operation
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Fresnel reflection at air-film and film-substrate interfaces
expected_advantages: Low layer count reduces deposition time and stress accumulation
Periodic structure is well-understood and reproducible
Symmetric design may reduce polarization sensitivity
known_risks: 8 layers may not provide sufficient MWIR suppression depth
Quarter-wave design optimized for one wavelength may have limited bandwidth
ZnSe not in guaranteed material catalog may require local resolution
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a periodic 8-layer multilayer film on Ge (Icenogle) substrate with air incidence. Stack order: Air | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | ZnS | ZnSe (Querry) | Ge (Icenogle). Two design variables: thickness_ZnS applies to layers 1,3,5,7; thickness_ZnSe (Querry) applies to layers 2,4,6,8. Wavelength bands: 8000-11000 nm (maximize transmittance), 3000-5000 nm (minimize transmittance). Total layers fixed at 8. Materials: zns, ZnSe (Querry), Ge (Icenogle). Find thickness values that maximize LWIR transmission while suppressing MWIR.

routes.title: Aperiodic 16-layer fully-optimized stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Free optimization of all 16 layer thicknesses without periodicity constraints can achieve superior spectral shaping compared to periodic designs, exploiting the full design space within the manufacturing limit.
routes.design_principle: Aperiodic multilayer optimization allows independent control of each interface's contribution to the spectral response, enabling custom spectral profiles that periodic structures cannot achieve. More degrees of freedom should enable better trade-offs between LWIR transmission and MWIR suppression.

routes.design_principle: Bragg reflector stopband depth increases with number of periods. Adding 2 more pairs should deepen MWIR suppression while maintaining LWIR transmission, testing whether intermediate layer counts offer better performance-manufacturability trade-off than 8 or 16 layers.

routes.title: Periodic ZnS/ZnSe Quarter-Wave Stack for MWIR Suppression with LWIR Pass
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 16-layer periodic stack of alternating ZnSe and ZnS, with optical thicknesses tuned to create a high-reflectance stopband centered near 4000 nm, will achieve transmittance above 80% in the 8000-11000 nm band while suppressing transmittance below 20% in the 3000-5000 nm band.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg reflectors produce maximum reflectance at the design wavelength where each layer has optical thickness λ/4. At wavelengths significantly longer than the design wavelength, the optical thickness becomes a smaller fraction of the wavelength, reducing the reflectance and allowing transmission. By centering the stopband at 4000 nm (middle of MWIR suppression band), the LWIR band (8000-11000 nm) falls in the transmission region beyond the stopband.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnSe(1) | ZnS(2) | ZnSe(3) | ZnS(4) | ZnSe(5) | ZnS(6) | ZnSe(7) | ZnS(8) | ZnSe(9) | ZnS(10) | ZnSe(11) | ZnS(12) | ZnSe(13) | ZnS(14) | ZnSe(15) | ZnS(16) | Ge substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 16 layers (t1 through t16 in nm)
Thickness ratio between ZnSe and ZnS layers within each pair
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band
Maintain smooth transmittance transition between bands to avoid sharp resonances
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 16 to meet the stated constraint
Layer thicknesses should remain above 200 nm for deposition uniformity
ZnSe and ZnS are both depositable by thermal evaporation or sputtering
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: ZnSe has higher refractive index than ZnS in the infrared region, providing moderate index contrast for Bragg reflection
Recalled knowledge: Germanium substrate has very high refractive index (~4.0 in IR), requiring anti-reflection consideration at the substrate interface
Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stack reflectance bandwidth scales with index contrast ratio; moderate contrast materials require more layers for deep suppression
Recalled knowledge: Absorption in ZnS and ZnSe is low in 3000-11000 nm range but increases toward longer wavelengths
Recalled design practice: Starting with high-index material at air interface improves match for high-reflector stacks
expected_advantages: Periodic structure simplifies optimization to thickness scaling rather than sequence search
16 layers provides sufficient pairs (8) for meaningful MWIR suppression with moderate index contrast
Quarter-wave centering at 4000 nm naturally creates LWIR passband without additional complexity
known_risks: Uncertain exact refractive index values for ZnS and ZnSe at 3000-11000 nm; actual index contrast may differ from recalled ~2.4 vs ~2.2
Uncertain whether Ge is resolvable in the material registry; if not, route will be rejected for repair
Uncertain absorption coefficients in LWIR band; ZnSe may have higher absorption than recalled at 11000 nm
16 layers may be insufficient for deep MWIR suppression if index contrast is lower than expected
No angle specification in request; assumed normal incidence but actual detector may have field-of-view requirements
The quarter-wave approach may create secondary transmission lobes in MWIR that reduce suppression effectiveness
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 16-layer planar multilayer dielectric film on Germanium substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence from air side: ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS (16 layers total, alternating starting with ZnSe (Querry)). Optimize individual layer thicknesses for all 16 layers to maximize transmittance in 8000-11000 nm wavelength band while minimizing transmittance in 3000-5000 nm wavelength band. Use normal incidence (0 degrees). Materials: ZnSe (Querry), zns, Ge (Icenogle). Total layer count is fixed at 16. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, run_status, and thicknesses_nm for each optimization round.

research_influence: L07 (Ge/ZnS multilayers for 2-15 µm) directly supports the material system choice for all three routes, confirming ZnS/Ge compatibility in the target wavelength range
L10 (Ge/ZnS filters on Ge and ZnSe substrates) validates the substrate and material combination, influencing the topology design for all routes
L12 (Anti-reflection for HgCdTe arrays) supports the detector application context, justifying the LWIR transmission priority
L13/L16 (Cryogenic IR filters) inform the manufacturing considerations regarding stress and thermal compatibility for cooled detector operation
unresolved_decisions: ZnSe is not in the guaranteed material catalog; local resolution will determine if it maps to exactly one dataset. If resolution fails, routes must be repaired with an alternative name from the rejection list
Incidence angle not specified by user; routes assume normal incidence (0 degrees) as default for window applications
Polarization state not specified; routes assume unpolarized or average of TE/TM as typical for detector windows
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all three routes fail to produce valid candidates with best_target_score above 0.3 after full optimization, the ZnS/ZnSe material pair on Ge substrate may be fundamentally unsuitable for this spectral requirement; recommend exploring alternative material pairs or relaxing the 16-layer constraint

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a periodic quarter-wave stack design, centered on the MWIR suppression band (3000-5000 nm), can simultaneously achieve high LWIR transmittance (8000-11000 nm) with only ZnS/ZnSe materials on Ge substrate within 16 layers. The design draws from recalled thin-film filter principles: a Bragg reflector centered at shorter wavelengths becomes increasingly transparent at longer wavelengths where optical thickness decreases. I would have wanted to look up exact n/k dispersion data for ZnS, ZnSe, and Ge across 3000-11000 nm to verify index contrast and absorption losses.

routes.title: Periodic ZnS/ZnSe Quarter-Wave Stack for MWIR Suppression with LWIR Pass
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 16-layer periodic stack of alternating ZnSe and ZnS, with optical thicknesses tuned to create a high-reflectance stopband centered near 4000 nm, will achieve transmittance above 80% in the 8000-11000 nm band while suppressing transmittance below 20% in the 3000-5000 nm band.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg reflectors produce maximum reflectance at the design wavelength where each layer has optical thickness λ/4. At wavelengths significantly longer than the design wavelength, the optical thickness becomes a smaller fraction of the wavelength, reducing the reflectance and allowing transmission. By centering the stopband at 4000 nm (middle of MWIR suppression band), the LWIR band (8000-11000 nm) falls in the transmission region beyond the stopband.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnSe(1) | ZnS(2) | ZnSe(3) | ZnS(4) | ZnSe(5) | ZnS(6) | ZnSe(7) | ZnS(8) | ZnSe(9) | ZnS(10) | ZnSe(11) | ZnS(12) | ZnSe(13) | ZnS(14) | ZnSe(15) | ZnS(16) | Ge substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 16 layers (t1 through t16 in nm)
Thickness ratio between ZnSe and ZnS layers within each pair
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band
Maintain smooth transmittance transition between bands to avoid sharp resonances
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 16 to meet the stated constraint
Layer thicknesses should remain above 200 nm for deposition uniformity
ZnSe and ZnS are both depositable by thermal evaporation or sputtering
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: ZnSe has higher refractive index than ZnS in the infrared region, providing moderate index contrast for Bragg reflection
Recalled knowledge: Germanium substrate has very high refractive index (~4.0 in IR), requiring anti-reflection consideration at the substrate interface
Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stack reflectance bandwidth scales with index contrast ratio; moderate contrast materials require more layers for deep suppression
Recalled knowledge: Absorption in ZnS and ZnSe is low in 3000-11000 nm range but increases toward longer wavelengths
Recalled design practice: Starting with high-index material at air interface improves match for high-reflector stacks
expected_advantages: Periodic structure simplifies optimization to thickness scaling rather than sequence search
16 layers provides sufficient pairs (8) for meaningful MWIR suppression with moderate index contrast
Quarter-wave centering at 4000 nm naturally creates LWIR passband without additional complexity
known_risks: Uncertain exact refractive index values for ZnS and ZnSe at 3000-11000 nm; actual index contrast may differ from recalled ~2.4 vs ~2.2
Uncertain whether Ge is resolvable in the material registry; if not, route will be rejected for repair
Uncertain absorption coefficients in LWIR band; ZnSe may have higher absorption than recalled at 11000 nm
16 layers may be insufficient for deep MWIR suppression if index contrast is lower than expected
No angle specification in request; assumed normal incidence but actual detector may have field-of-view requirements
The quarter-wave approach may create secondary transmission lobes in MWIR that reduce suppression effectiveness
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 16-layer planar multilayer dielectric film on Germanium substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence from air side: ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS (16 layers total, alternating starting with ZnSe (Querry)). Optimize individual layer thicknesses for all 16 layers to maximize transmittance in 8000-11000 nm wavelength band while minimizing transmittance in 3000-5000 nm wavelength band. Use normal incidence (0 degrees). Materials: ZnSe (Querry), zns, Ge (Icenogle). Total layer count is fixed at 16. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, run_status, and thicknesses_nm for each optimization round.
